slides.title: Why not just **read()** each client?
bullets: 🧊|Blocking `read()` stalls on the first idle socket

slides.title: `select` checks **everyone**, every time
bullets: 📋|Copies the whole fd set into the kernel each call
🔁|You rebuild the set before every call
🔍|Then you scan all fds to find the ready ones

cols.title: 🟰 Level
cols.text: Keeps reporting while data remains. Safe. Redis uses this.

cols.title: ⚡ Edge
cols.text: Reports on change only. Read until EAGAIN or lose data.

slides.title: epoll is not **magic**
bullets: 🧰|Used by Redis, Nginx, Node.js (libuv) on Linux
🤏|Under ~100 sockets, select is just as fast

slides.title: Say this in 1 line
slides.text: `select` re-scans **every fd on every call**, O(n), capped at 1,024. `epoll` **registers once** and returns **only ready fds**, O(ready). That is how one thread serves thousands of idle connections.
